reason: Both Updates address behavior that the supplied runs actually exhibit (long one-type searches with revisits, and wasted no-op steps). Only u1 needs refinement: the current evidence and Memory M3/M6 show that the effective ingredient is sampling additional receptacle types plus exact-target/no-substitute guidance, while the anti-cycling/revisit-avoidance wording alone was not reliably followed and is hard to track with the Actor's two-step history. u2 already matches the recorded no-op evidence (unreachable 'go to', duplicate 'look', empty-handed 'inventory'), so it is preserved, and the existing Checks remain appropriate.

to.text: During any search for the exact requested object (or, once the target is in hand, for the desklamp), do not restrict the search to one container type or to a small set of locations. When the current observation shows the exact requested item is absent, choose the next destination from the admissible 'go to' list so that you sample a receptacle type not yet used in this search rather than another instance of the type just swept or a location you just saw was empty; for example, if a run of drawers has not yielded the target, go to cabinets, countertops, shelves, fridge, diningtable, or sinkbasin before re-entering the drawer series. While sweeping the numbered instances of one container type, move in one direction and do not return to an instance you just left empty. Keep the existing rule to open a closed cabinet/drawer/fridge on arrival and inspect its contents before leaving. Continue until the exact target is found or every receptacle type available in the room's action list has been sampled once. This is coverage for finding the exact target within the step budget; it does not permit picking up, conditioning, or placing a substitute object.

adjustments.reason: Current runs show the Actor confines long searches to one or two receptacle types and revisits empty ones: P6 sweeps drawers up to drawer 20 and never opens a cabinet (P6:6, P6:50), P8 cycles among cabinets and sinkbasin and never reaches shelf 1 (P8:9, P8:50), and P10 cycles among fridge/countertops/cabinets for many steps before finding the apple (P10:6). Memory M3/M6 record that the anti-cycling/revisit-avoidance wording was not reliably followed and did not by itself break the cycling/step-limit failure, whereas added search breadth combined with exact-target guidance did help. The revised Update therefore makes the breadth requirement executable from the recent observations and the admissible 'go to' list, prioritizes sampling untried receptacle types, and retains the one-direction sweep, the open-closed-container rule, and the no-substitute constraint.
